name: Credit Card Fraud Detection (ULB / Worldline)
license: Database Contents License (DbCL) v1.0; free Kaggle login
gives: 284,807 European card transactions over two days with 492 frauds; a clean imbalanced benchmark for model and metric code
caveat: Features are PCA-anonymised and only 48 hours long: no velocity windows, merchants or label delay

name: IEEE-CIS Fraud Detection
gives: About 590K e-commerce transactions with card, address, email-domain and device fields over six months
caveat: Columns are masked and identity is joined by a hashed key; build time-based splits

name: PaySim synthetic mobile-money transactions
license: See the dataset page; free Kaggle login
gives: 6.3M simulated transfers with sender and recipient accounts
caveat: Simulated from one company's logs, so patterns are simpler than production

name: Home Credit Default Risk
gives: Loan applications with bureau, instalment and credit-card history tables for default prediction
caveat: Many linked tables and heavy missingness; join with care to avoid leakage

name: Give Me Some Credit
gives: 150,000 borrowers with delinquency outcomes, a small clean credit-scoring benchmark
caveat: Few features and no time axis; use it to test the scoring and calibration code only

name: Statlog German Credit Data (UCI)
gives: 1,000 credit applicants with a good or bad label and a cost matrix
caveat: Tiny and old; useful for fairness and explainability exercises, not scale

name: Elliptic Bitcoin transaction graph
license: See the dataset page; free Kaggle login
gives: 200K Bitcoin transactions as a graph with licit and illicit labels and temporal steps
caveat: Anonymised features; labels cover only part of the graph

name: IBM AMLSim (anti-money-laundering simulator)
gives: A simulator that generates transaction networks with injected laundering patterns
caveat: Synthetic; patterns reflect the simulator's assumptions

name: Porto Seguro Safe Driver Prediction
gives: 600K insurance policies with anonymised features and a claim-filed label
caveat: Anonymised features limit domain feature work

name: Jane Street Market Prediction
gives: Anonymised market features with returns and a trade-or-not decision target
caveat: Anonymised and from one firm; check the data terms

name: FinancialPhraseBank
gives: About 4,800 financial news sentences labelled positive, neutral or negative
caveat: Small and sentence-level; limited to financial news

name: Retailrocket recommender system dataset
gives: About 2.7 million view, add-to-cart and purchase events with item properties
caveat: Anonymised ids and no dwell time

name: RecSys Challenge 2015 (YooChoose clicks and buys)
license: See the dataset page; free Kaggle login
gives: About 33 million click events in sessions with purchase outcomes
caveat: Old (2014) and coarse categories; keep a strict time split

name: Amazon-M2 multilingual shopping sessions
license: See the paper for the licence
gives: Anonymised multi-locale shopping sessions with product attributes for next-item prediction
caveat: Several locales with different catalogues; evaluate each separately

name: Instacart Market Basket Analysis
gives: 3 million grocery orders from 200K users with reorder labels
caveat: No timestamps beyond day-of-week and hour; US grocery only

name: H&M Personalized Fashion Recommendations
gives: Two years of purchases with article metadata and images for next-purchase recommendation
caveat: Large; fashion-specific seasonality

name: Olist Brazilian E-Commerce
gives: 100K orders with items, payments, reviews, delivery times and seller data
caveat: One marketplace and year; useful for delivery, review and seller analyses

name: Amazon Reviews 2023
license: Research terms on the project page
gives: Hundreds of millions of product reviews with item metadata across categories
caveat: Very large; consumer-review language and bias

name: MovieLens datasets
gives: Explicit ratings from 100K to 25M with timestamps, the standard recommender benchmark
caveat: Explicit ratings are not implicit clicks; film domain

name: UCI Online Retail
gives: About 540K invoices from a UK gift retailer over a year
caveat: Single retailer, no sessions; good for RFM, churn and basket work

name: M5 Forecasting - Accuracy (Walmart)
gives: Five years of daily unit sales for about 30,000 item-store series with prices, promotions and calendar events
caveat: Intermittent series and no order-book or weather signals

name: Corporacion Favorita Grocery Sales Forecasting
gives: Daily sales for thousands of items across 54 stores with promotions, holidays and oil prices
caveat: Real stock-outs are unlabelled

name: Rossmann Store Sales
gives: Daily sales for 1,115 drugstores with promotion, holiday and competitor features
caveat: Store-level totals, not SKU level

name: PhysioNet / Computing in Cardiology Challenge 2019: Early Prediction of Sepsis
gives: Hourly vitals, labs and a sepsis label for about 40,000 ICU patients
caveat: Labels are rule-derived and the two hospital systems differ in sampling

name: MIMIC-IV
license: PhysioNet Credentialed Health Data License; credentialing required
gives: De-identified hospital and ICU stays with vitals, labs, medications and procedures
caveat: Credentialed access; single centre

name: eICU Collaborative Research Database
license: PhysioNet Credentialed Health Data License; credentialing required
gives: ICU stays from many US hospitals, for cross-site testing
caveat: Credentialed access; coding differs by hospital

name: Diabetes 130-US Hospitals (UCI)
gives: 100K inpatient encounters with a 30-day readmission outcome
caveat: Old data and coarse features

name: UCI Heart Disease
gives: Small clinical dataset with a heart-disease label
caveat: Tiny; use only to test pipeline and calibration code

name: MedMNIST
license: CC BY 4.0 per dataset (see the site)
gives: Standardised small medical image datasets for classification and segmentation across modalities
caveat: Low resolution; for prototyping, not clinical performance claims

name: RSNA Pneumonia Detection Challenge
gives: Chest X-rays with bounding boxes for pneumonia opacities
caveat: Label noise and one source; check the terms

name: Diabetic Retinopathy Detection
gives: Retinal images graded for diabetic retinopathy severity
caveat: Variable image quality and grader noise

name: ISIC Archive (skin lesion images)
gives: Dermoscopic images with diagnoses from the International Skin Imaging Collaboration
caveat: Site and device differences; skin-tone coverage is uneven

name: MoleculeNet
gives: A benchmark collection of molecular property datasets (toxicity, solubility, binding)
caveat: Benchmark splits can be optimistic; use scaffold splits

name: Therapeutics Data Commons
gives: Curated datasets across drug discovery tasks, including drug-drug interaction and ADMET
caveat: Heterogeneous quality; read each dataset's notes

name: PubMedQA
gives: Biomedical research questions with abstracts and yes/no/maybe answers
caveat: Research abstracts, not clinical notes

name: DataCo Smart Supply Chain
license: See the dataset page; free Kaggle login
gives: 180K order lines with shipping modes, delivery status, late-delivery risk and customers
caveat: Synthetic-looking and single company; use for pipeline work

name: Amazon Last Mile Routing Research Challenge
gives: Real delivery routes with stop sequences and driver behaviour for routing research
caveat: US urban routes in 2018; routes only, no demand

name: CVRPLIB (vehicle routing benchmarks)
gives: Standard capacitated vehicle routing instances with best-known solutions
caveat: Benchmarks have static, deterministic costs

name: OR-Library
license: Free for research use (see the site)
gives: A collection of operations research test instances: scheduling, packing, location, assignment
caveat: Old formats; classic benchmarks only

name: MIPLIB 2017
gives: A library of mixed-integer programming instances for testing optimisers
caveat: Hard to relate to a specific business problem

name: NYC Taxi and Limousine Commission trip records (AWS Open Data)
gives: Hundreds of millions of trip records with pickup and drop-off times, locations and fares
caveat: One city; no driver identities

name: NASA Prognostics Data Repository (C-MAPSS and others)
gives: Run-to-failure sensor data for engines and other components
caveat: Simulated or lab data; real fleets are messier

name: Criteo Display Advertising Challenge
gives: About 45 million display-ad impressions with 13 numeric and 26 hashed categorical features and a click label
caveat: No position, timestamp or user id

name: Avazu Click-Through Rate Prediction
gives: About 40 million mobile ad impressions over 10 days with hourly timestamps
caveat: No position or dwell time

name: Criteo AI Lab datasets
license: Research-use terms on the Criteo AI Lab page
gives: Large click logs, uplift, attribution and counterfactual datasets from Criteo
caveat: Terabyte scale for some sets; research-use terms

name: Open Bandit Dataset
gives: Logged bandit feedback from a fashion e-commerce site with propensities, for off-policy evaluation
caveat: One platform and a short period

name: TalkingData AdTracking Fraud Detection
gives: 200 million mobile ad clicks with an app-download label to detect click fraud
caveat: Anonymised and from one platform

name: KDD Cup 2012 Track 2: ad click prediction
gives: Search-ad impressions with query, ad, user and position fields
caveat: Old and anonymised, but it records the display position

name: CIC-IDS2017 intrusion detection
license: Research use with citation (see the page)
gives: Labelled network flows with benign traffic and common attacks over five days
caveat: Lab traffic; known labelling issues in places

name: UNSW-NB15
license: Research use with citation (see the page)
gives: Network packets and flows with modern attack types and labels
caveat: Synthetic attack generation; class imbalance varies by split

name: EMBER malware dataset
gives: 1 million Windows PE file feature vectors with benign and malicious labels and a time split
caveat: Features, not raw files; labelling cut-off artefacts

name: UCI Phishing Websites
gives: 11,000 websites with URL and page features and a phishing label
caveat: Static features from one period; attackers adapt

name: Splunk Boss of the SOC v3 (BOTS)
gives: A realistic corpus of security logs from a simulated attack with a question set that gives ground truth
caveat: One scenario, Splunk format

name: OTRF Security-Datasets (Mordor)
gives: Pre-recorded telemetry for individual attack techniques mapped to MITRE ATT&CK
caveat: Lab-generated, little benign background

name: LANL Comprehensive Multi-Source Cyber-Security Events
license: Research release from Los Alamos National Laboratory (see the page)
gives: 58 days of authentication, process, flow and DNS events with a red-team subset
caveat: Anonymised and very large

name: NSL-KDD
license: Research use with citation (see the page)
gives: A cleaned version of the classic KDD Cup 99 intrusion data
caveat: Very old; use only to test code

name: NVD vulnerability data feeds
gives: All published CVEs with descriptions, severity scores and affected products
caveat: Severity is not exploitation; label exploitation from another source

name: EPSS data and statistics
license: Free to use with attribution (see the page)
gives: Daily exploit prediction scores for all CVEs with historical data
caveat: Predicts exploitation probability, which you may want to improve on

name: Enron email dataset
gives: About 500,000 emails from 150 users
caveat: Old corporate email; legal and privacy sensitivities

name: Riiid Answer Correctness Prediction (EdNet-based)
gives: About 100 million answers from roughly 400,000 students with timestamps and question tags
caveat: Anonymised and large; split by student

name: EdNet (Santa tutoring service)
gives: Interaction logs from more than 780,000 users over two years
caveat: Non-commercial licence and very large

name: ASSISTments public datasets
license: Research terms on each dataset page
gives: Maths tutoring logs with skill ids, correctness and attempt counts
caveat: Known duplicates and ordering issues in older releases

name: Open University Learning Analytics Dataset (OULAD)
gives: Student demographics, VLE click streams and outcomes for 32,000 students
caveat: UK distance learning; coarse click aggregation

name: UCI Predict Students' Dropout and Academic Success
gives: 4,400 students with enrolment and early-performance features and a dropout label
caveat: One institution; small

name: ASAP Automated Student Assessment Prize: essay scoring
gives: Student essays with human scores across eight prompts
caveat: Prompt-specific; scores from one era

name: ASAP-SAS short answer scoring
gives: Short student answers with human scores for ten prompts
caveat: Prompt-specific and small per prompt

name: Duolingo half-life regression data
gives: Learner review logs with recall outcomes for spaced-repetition modelling
caveat: One app and language-learning domain

name: IBM Project CodeNet
gives: 14 million code submissions across 55 languages with problem and verdict metadata
caveat: Competitive-programming style, not course assignments

name: RACE reading comprehension
gives: About 28,000 passages and 100,000 exam questions from English exams for Chinese students
caveat: Exam questions, one population

name: Mozilla Common Voice
gives: Crowd-sourced speech recordings with transcripts in many languages
caveat: Read speech; accents and noise vary

name: Telco Customer Churn
license: See the dataset page; free Kaggle login
gives: 7,000 subscribers with services, contract and churn label
caveat: Small, one telco, no time axis

name: KKBox Churn Prediction Challenge
gives: Subscription and listening logs for a music service with a churn label
caveat: Music streaming, not B2B SaaS

name: GH Archive
gives: Hourly public GitHub events: pushes, pull requests, issues and reviews
caveat: Public repositories only; bot noise

name: SWE-bench
gives: Real GitHub issues with the pull requests that fixed them and runnable tests
caveat: Python repositories only

name: HumanEval
gives: 164 hand-written programming problems with unit tests for evaluating code generation
caveat: Small and widely contaminated; use for harness checks

name: CodeSearchNet
license: MIT licence plus per-project licences (see the repository)
gives: About 2 million functions with natural-language documentation in six languages
caveat: Docstrings are not user queries

name: Spider text-to-SQL
gives: 10,000 questions with SQL over 200 databases for cross-domain text-to-SQL
caveat: Clean academic schemas, simpler than production

name: BIRD text-to-SQL benchmark
gives: A large benchmark of questions over big, messy databases with external knowledge
caveat: Execution cost is high

name: Loghub system log collection
gives: Real log datasets from distributed systems, supercomputers and applications
caveat: Labels are sparse and system-specific

name: Numenta Anomaly Benchmark (NAB)
gives: 58 labelled real and synthetic time series for streaming anomaly detection with a scoring scheme
caveat: Small and labels are debated

name: Server Machine Dataset (OmniAnomaly)
gives: Multivariate server metrics from an internet company with labelled anomalies
caveat: One company; coarse labels

name: Azure Public Dataset
gives: Anonymised VM, workload and resource utilisation traces from Azure
caveat: One cloud and period

name: Google cluster data
gives: Production cluster traces with job events, resource usage and failures
caveat: Dated; Google-specific scheduling

name: MS MARCO
gives: Large-scale passage and document ranking data from real search queries
caveat: Web search, not enterprise or docs

name: BEIR benchmark
gives: A heterogeneous benchmark of 18 retrieval datasets for zero-shot evaluation
caveat: Academic tasks; domain match varies

name: Banking77 intent dataset
gives: 13,000 customer banking queries labelled with 77 intents
caveat: Short single-turn queries

name: Customer Support on Twitter
license: See the dataset page; free Kaggle login
gives: About 3 million tweets and replies between customers and company support accounts
caveat: Public social posts; informal language

name: Jigsaw Toxic Comment Classification
gives: 160K Wikipedia comments labelled for several kinds of toxicity
caveat: Wikipedia talk pages; labelling bias

name: CoNLL-2003 named entity recognition
gives: Newswire text tagged with person, organisation, location and miscellaneous entities
caveat: News text; short entity vocabulary

name: GoEmotions
gives: 58,000 Reddit comments labelled with 27 emotion categories
caveat: Reddit language; label subjectivity

name: Open Graph Benchmark
gives: Large realistic graph datasets for node, link and graph prediction with standard splits
caveat: Academic graphs; business graphs are messier

name: Stanford SNAP network datasets
gives: A large collection of social, web and transaction networks
caveat: Mostly social networks

name: DeepMatcher entity-matching datasets
gives: Labelled record pairs for entity matching across products, publications and companies
caveat: Small to medium pairs sets

name: Web Data Commons product corpus
gives: Millions of product offers from the web with identifiers for product matching
caveat: Web-scraped and noisy

name: OpenML
gives: Thousands of versioned tabular datasets with tasks and benchmarks
caveat: Mostly small and clean

name: UCI Machine Learning Repository
gives: A long-standing archive of small and medium datasets across domains
caveat: Small and old; good for code, weak for realism

name: Monash Time Series Forecasting Archive
gives: A curated archive of forecasting datasets across domains with standard splits
caveat: Benchmarks, not your data

name: UCR Time Series Archive
license: Research use with citation (see the page)
gives: 128 labelled time-series classification datasets
caveat: Short curated series

name: ETT electricity transformer dataset
gives: Multivariate transformer temperature and load data used for long-horizon forecasting benchmarks
caveat: One asset type

name: COCO common objects
license: Annotations CC BY 4.0; images under Flickr terms
gives: 330K images with object detection, segmentation and caption annotations
caveat: Everyday objects, not your domain

name: SKU-110K retail shelf detection
license: Academic and non-commercial use (see the repository)
gives: About 11,700 shelf images with over a million densely packed product boxes
caveat: Academic-use licence

name: DeepFashion
gives: Over 800,000 fashion images with categories, attributes, landmarks and consumer-to-shop pairs
caveat: Non-commercial; fashion-only

name: FUNSD form understanding
gives: 199 scanned forms annotated for entity and relation extraction
caveat: Tiny; English forms

name: DocVQA
gives: Question answering over document images with text and layout
caveat: Mostly English business documents
